proof_attempt_summary: The uniform critical-radius frontier was rejected for overlap; a distinct affine-family two-price classification was proposed, then strengthened to matching linear transport, variance and Gaussian interval-length sensitivity. D0.5 graded the delivered restricted package incremental with score ceiling 6.4 below the field gate 7.4, and both boundary and independent terminal consults confirmed downgraded banking without lowering the floor. No Lean formalization ran; a jointly stationary global-mark Campbell bridge, targeted public collision audit, endpoint assembly and executed numerical calibration remain unresolved.
tldr: For the declared nonnegative conditional sample ATE optimizer at \(C_n(c)=c\sqrt n\), two scalar prices share limiting precision exactly when one stationary load field satisfies the transfer inequalities at both prices. In the note\textquotesingle s nonconstant affine recruitment family with fair assignment, distance decrease and variance increase have matching linear bounds in the price difference. The price--radius relation makes limiting variance and scaled Gaussian interval length bi-Lipschitz on every corresponding compact radius interval, with explicit constants uniform over the family. The ninth-order rational event bound is an exact positivity certificate; the linear theorem gives the sharp sensitivity order. Established stationary, spatial, empirical, and Gaussian inference results connect this sensitivity to the observed optimizer.
gap: The banked manuscript already records the smooth-density spatial frontier as a surviving seed. It does not classify common load fields at two prices or supply quantitative interior sensitivity. Published causal weighting results and prescribed-marginal stationary transport leave this distinction unresolved.
fill: A necessary-and-sufficient stationary transfer system, a robust five-point obstruction, an explicit compact-interval separation bound and an executable rational certificate classify the interior price path. Supporting spatial limits transfer the result to reported causal interval precision.
